Every model is used below; read the values as a description of all models, not of a kept set. cat(methods_text(sensitivity), sep = "\n\n") #> We described the sensitivity of the matched design to the propensity model with the R package propsens (version 0.1.0). Propensity models from logistic regression, random forest and gradient boosting (1 seed for each tree method; 3 models; 5-fold cross-fitted scores; seed 1) were each used for 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching with replacement. Models were kept if their cross-fitted log-loss was within 5 % of the best model's and their largest post-match standardized mean difference on main terms was within 0.10 of the best model's and at most 0.25; fewer than two of the 3 models met these criteria, so all models were used, and all treated patients were matched. For all models we report the mean rank disagreement over treated patients, the bootstrap rank instability of the logistic model, and the range of the largest standardized mean difference on main terms. No outcome data were used. These summaries are descriptive; they have not been validated as predictors of bias. #>  #> Mean rank disagreement over treated patients was 0.069 across all models; the bootstrap rank instability of the logistic model was 0.036. As exploratory summaries, pair instability was 0.63 (of a possible 0.67 with 3 models) and the median between/within-algorithm ratio was not available. The largest standardized mean difference on main terms ranged from 0.16 to 0.54 across all models.
